A Morningstar report says the recent volatility in the bond market has created “one of the most compelling opportunities in years”.

Structural demand is supporting infrastructure growth, according to Preqin’s “Private Markets in 2031” report.

Global insurers plan to up their allocations to private markets, according to a BlackRock survey.

The Growth Equity Strategies Team at Loomis Sayles, an affiliate of Natixis Investment Managers, demonstrates that patience, discipline and conviction result in consistent, peer-leading risk-adjusted compounding over cycles.

AllianzGI, Allspring and BlackRock predict a delay in rate hikes at the next Fed meeting, but not an end to monetary tightening.

Robeco’s value manager Wim-Hein Pals took profits in tech when the market “was going ballistic”.

Hang Seng Bank has onboarded the BNP Paribas Asset Management funds to its wealth management platform.

The collaboration aims develop ETFs across Hong Kong, UCITS, and US ETF structures.

Ryuji Katayama will oversee PGIM’s real estate business in Japan.

PGIM has promoted Ryuji Katayama to head of Japan, real estate as it seeks to expand the growth of its business in the region.

Katayama was most recently deputy head of Japan for real estate at PGIM and was instrumental in scaling PGIM’s Asia Pacific real estate investment platform, including the expansion of its flagship Asia Pacific value-add (AVP) strategies, the firm said.

He is to continue his role as portfolio manager for the AVP and Japan-focused investment strategies, PGIM added.

Katayama will be based in Tokyo and reporting to David Fassbender, PGIM’s head of Asia Pacific, real estate.

“Japan is one of our highest-conviction markets globally and a key pillar of our long-term growth strategy in Asia Pacific,” Fassbender said. “Ryuji is an accomplished investor and leader who has played an important role in strengthening PGIM’s investment platform in Japan and across the region.”

“His deep market expertise, investment acumen and breadth of long-standing relationships will be integral to helping investors navigate the next market cycle and advancing our business in the market.”

Katayama joined PGIM in 2012, where prior to becoming deputy head for real estate, he was head of transactions, Japan, for PGIM’s real estate investment group.

Prior to joining PGIM, he was with ORIX in Tokyo, where he focused on direct real estate equity investments and non-performing loan transactions.

PGIM’s real estate investment group runs $219 billion in gross real estate assets under management and administration globally.

FSA highlights 5 healthcare exchange-traded-funds that are outpacing the S&P 500 index year-to-date.
